name: Luna 15
short_status: Failure: crashed in Mare Crisium on 21 July 1969 at about 15:50 UT, roughly two hours before Apollo 11 lifted off from the Moon, ending the Soviet attempt to return lunar soil before the Americans got home.
tagline: Soviet Union · Sample return · 1969 · The space race Failure
stats: of lunar soil returned: the descent ended in a crash
lunar orbits before the failed landing attempt
before Apollo 11 lifted off from the Moon
from the Apollo 11 landing site, in Mare Crisium

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 13 July 1969, 02:54:42 UTC, on a Proton-K/Blok D from Baikonur (Site 81/24); vehicle Ye-8-5 no. 401

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: Ye-8-5 robotic sample-return station, 5,667 kg at launch, 2,718 kg dry; same design family as the later successful Luna 16, 20 and 24

facts.label: Objective
facts.value: Land, drill lunar soil, and return a capsule to Earth before Apollo 11 got home, so the USSR could claim the first lunar sample even after losing the crewed landing

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: 17 July 1969, one day before Apollo 11 landed; final orbit about 110 km by 16 km, inclination 127 degrees, period 1 h 54 min

facts.label: Orbit operations
facts.value: 52 orbits of the Moon and 86 communication sessions; two orbit-correction burns lowered the perilune ahead of the landing attempt

facts.label: Landing delayed
facts.value: Soviet controllers held Luna 15 in orbit an extra day past the planned 20 July landing, uneasy about the ruggedness of the target site

facts.label: Deorbit and loss of signal
facts.value: 21 July 1969: descent engine fired at 18:46:43 Moscow time (15:46:43 UT); signal ceased at 18:50:40 Moscow time (15:50:40 UT), about 237 seconds into the descent

facts.label: Crash
facts.value: Impacted Mare Crisium at about 15:50 UT, at a published point near 17 N, 60 E, roughly 1,200 km east-northeast of Tranquility Base

facts.label: Probable cause
facts.value: NASA's account: the craft descended at excessive speed, apparently because its attitude when the descent engine fired was off by several degrees; a competing account has it striking high ground in the mare

facts.label: Unprecedented data exchange
facts.value: Apollo 8 commander Frank Borman contacted Academician Mstislav Keldysh, who provided Luna 15's planned trajectory and confirmed its orbit did not cross Apollo 11's, the first such Soviet-American exchange

facts.label: Jodrell Bank tracking
facts.value: Bernard Lovell's team at Jodrell Bank tracked Luna 15 alongside Apollo 11; a recording of the control room during the crash was released publicly on 3 July 2009

facts.label: Earlier attempt
facts.value: The preceding Ye-8-5 no. 402 failed to reach Earth orbit at launch on 14 June 1969, one month before Luna 15

timeline: The preceding Ye-8-5 no. 402 fails to reach orbit at launch, leaving Luna 15 as the Soviet bid to upstage Apollo 11
02:54:42 UTC: Launch on a Proton-K/Blok D from Baikonur, three days before Apollo 11
Enters lunar orbit, a day ahead of Apollo 11's arrival at the Moon
Frank Borman relays Luna 15's orbit from Academician Keldysh, who confirms it will not cross Apollo 11's path
Two orbit-correction burns lower the perilune, but controllers postpone the landing past 20 July, wary of the terrain
15:46:43 UT: Descent engine fires; signal is lost at 15:50:40 UT and Luna 15 crashes in Mare Crisium, about two hours before Apollo 11 leaves the Moon
Jodrell Bank releases its control-room recording of the tracking and crash, forty years on
